By using the maximum allowable catalyst concentration (0.20) and maximum substrate concentration (5.0), we will drastically amplify second-order catalyst interactions (such as dimerization in M2, M3, or bimolecular deactivation in M13, M18, M19). A 20-fold increase in catalyst concentration compared to the previous experiment will cause second-order rates to increase by a factor of 400, which first-order models will struggle to fit simultaneously. Furthermore, saturating the system with substrate will shift the resting state of the catalyst almost entirely to the `catS` complex. This will strongly differentiate mechanisms that depend on free catalyst deactivation (M9, M11, M12) from those dependent on `catS` deactivation (M14, M16, M18) or higher-order substrate binding (M7). Setting initial product to 0.0 ensures we are observing these primary dynamics without the confounding effects of product inhibition early in the reaction.
</hypothesis>
